about: Drafted by dev@ from Dinis's guidance of 16 and 18 November 2026, for journalist@ to revise: one entry per principle or concept, each with what we do, what we never do and how to check us.
intro: These are the standards we judge ourselves by, and the ones others can judge us by. Each has its own page: what we do, what we never do and how you can check us. Where something is planned and not yet done, the page says so.

concepts.title: The register of sources
concepts.summary: We keep one list of every source we read, with what it gives and whose terms apply.
do: List every data point and news publication on one register: what it is and what it would give each place.
Record whether we read it today, with its terms or robots.txt quoted, linked and dated.
Show two views: the sources we use, and the sources we do not use today.
Start with official and public bodies.
never: Never read a source whose terms or robots.txt say no.
Never assume a source is open because it is public.

concepts.title: Sources we do not read
concepts.summary: We publish the list of sources we could read but do not, and why, and we respect what they say.
do: Say why each source is not read, quoting its terms or robots.txt with the link and the date read.
Ask each one on the record whether a site like this may show its public data.
Record the answer, or the lack of one, with its date.
Show only the title, date, place and link for an item found only on such a source, as a search engine does.
never: Never work around a refusal.
Never copy from a source that does not allow it.

concepts.title: Licences on everything
concepts.summary: Every piece of data shows its licence, and what we make is Creative Commons.
do: Publish our own pages, data and visualisations under CC BY 4.0.
Keep what we take from others under their licence, with a link on every item.
Link the source's terms, in those words, where it publishes no licence.
Credit how we found an item, for example a search service.
never: Never leave a licence blank.
Never assume a source is open.

concepts.title: People who publish in public
concepts.summary: We name and link people who publish in public, and we never touch what is private.
do: Name people in public office and anyone who publishes under their own name, such as a blogger.
Link their published words and attribute them by the name they published under.
Collect blogs, newsletters and podcasts through their public feeds.
Take a piece down on request, and let a source claim its entry to correct or opt out.
never: Never publish private information: home, family, health.
Never publish a personal contact.
Never use anything behind a login.

concepts.title: Evidence, and details withheld
concepts.summary: Every claim carries its evidence, and we hold back detail that could cause harm.
do: Attach a source, a link and a date read to each fact.
Show an open security finding by title, severity and state only.
Say plainly when we hold something back, and why.
For cyber signals, show aggregates and totals only.
never: Never publish a list of IPs, hosts or devices.
Never publish detail that would let someone exploit an open finding.

concepts.title: Submissions
concepts.summary: An organiser's own submission is published, credited and dated as theirs.
do: Publish what an organiser sends, credited to them and dated.
Take submissions through a public GitHub issue.
Add signing with the organiser's key later, as we go.
never: Never publish a third party's submission on its word alone: it is a lead to confirm.
Never present a submission as our own finding.

concepts.title: Take-downs and corrections
concepts.summary: If something is wrong or should not be here, tell us and we act in the open.
do: Offer three ways to report: a public issue, an encrypted drop, and a monitored agent inbox.
Look at each report, answer it, change what is wrong and record it.
Keep a corrections log without the reporter's details.
Leave out a source that asks to be left out.
never: Never ignore a report.
Never record who reported in the corrections log.

concepts.title: Security findings are published
concepts.summary: We keep a public log of every vulnerability, bug and breach, ours included.
do: Log each finding with severity, site and file, when found, the fix and its state.
Publish a fixed finding in full.
Give each site its own security page with its threat models.
Keep the log true at each wake of the security agent.
never: Never hide a breach because it is ours.
Never publish exploit detail while a finding is open.

concepts.title: Inner passes at every wake
concepts.summary: Every agent checks its own work in a fixed order before it commits.
do: Open with a conductor pass, then a security pre-review.
Do the work, then a security post-review of the diff.
Close with a conductor pass: status, report and any block.
Add an application security review whenever the diff touches code.
never: Never commit a secret, a private person's data or a contact.
Never work around a refusal.

concepts.title: Threat models for what runs on its own
concepts.summary: Every collector and automation has a published threat model.
do: Write a threat model per collector, scheduled workflow and drop: what it reads, writes and trusts.
List what could go wrong and the mitigations.
Have the security agent review each one.
Run a prompt-injection pass at least daily.
never: Never let an automation run without a threat model.
Never act on instructions found in fetched text.

concepts.title: Agent Behaviour Policies
concepts.summary: Every agent has a written policy for what it may do, tightened as it runs.
do: Give each agent its own policy in board/abp/.
Start new agents on a relaxed default and lock long-running ones down.
Map each run: tool calls, refusals and breaches.
Write plain case studies of notable events.
never: Never relax a policy without Dinis.
Never treat a relayed instruction as one from Dinis.

concepts.title: Telemetry
concepts.summary: One side-car agent measures what the agents spend and call, and the totals are public.
do: Track tokens, cost, tools and hosts called per agent and run.
Keep raw detail in an encrypted vault.
Publish aggregates only.
Say what telemetry cannot see: the network proxy's own logs.
never: Never let another session read transcripts.
Never put raw detail in the public repository.

concepts.title: Simulated payouts to sources
concepts.summary: We model how revenue could be shared with sources, and say it is only a simulation.
do: Mark every page: no payment is made or collected.
State the model's assumptions, for Dinis to change.
Compute "my five pounds" in the reader's browser.
Wait for Dinis on how much to keep and when anyone is paid.
never: Never send anything about the reader to us.
Never present the simulation as real payments.

concepts.title: The pipeline standard
concepts.summary: Every source goes through the same steps, so anyone can see what we do with its data.
do: Keep the raw data as received, timestamped and never overwritten.
Turn it into JSON with source, licence and read time.
Add a visualisation and an analysis.
Give each source a home page and an OpenAPI, listed in one Swagger of Swaggers.
never: Never overwrite history.
Never copy a source's content: we link.
